newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindu party stalls Indian parliament over Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Hindu party stalls Indian parliament over Pakistan.

text.p: India's main Hindu opposition party on Thursday stalled proceedings in parliament over proposed talks with Pakistan, saying New Delhi must not give unilateral concessions to its Islamic neighbour.
"There should be no unilateral concessions. Why should there be no reciprocity?" said Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) deputy Pramod Mahajan, forcing a brief adjournment of the lower house of parliament.
"We want to know from the government why the proposed visa relaxation the foreign minister has announced cannot be linked with the release of Indian soldiers in Pakistani prisons," Mahajan said.

Indian officials quoted Foreign Minister Inder Gujral as saying he proposed to relax restrictions on visas for Pakistani businessmen and journalists to boost people-to-people contact between the neighbours, who have fought three wars since 1947.
Top-level talks, stalled since January 1994, are scheduled to begin in New Delhi on March 28. Gujral told Reuters on Wednesday he proposed to open up trade with Pakistan.
The BJP, a hardline Hindu nationalist party, opposes talks with Pakistan unless they include the issue of "terrorism" that it alleges Islamabad promotes in the disputed territory of Kashmir.
The two neighbours have gone to war twice over Kashmir, of which India controls two-thirds and Pakistan the rest.

Pakistan, which says it provides only moral and diplomatic support to separatist rebels in the Himalayan region, regards progress in resolving the dispute over Kashmir as a prerequisite for talks on other issues.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is due to meet his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, on the sidelines of a regional summit in the Maldives in May.
Gujral is scheduled to meet Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan at a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement in April in New Delhi.
